main_body: Thatched hall: a large straw roof slope (rows ~4-54) over a timber plank wall with a central doorway (rows ~50-78)
top_band: Golden-straw roof slope, rows ~4-52, in layered light-to-mid ochre courses with dark separator lines; a darker brown eave line sits at rows ~50-54
evidence: In the middle column the roof thatch is a tall, clearly visible sloped surface. Its overhanging eave ends in a darker edge row, and below it is a shaded zone before the vertical plank wall. The wall has a stone footing and a framed doorway with a dark interior, and the door posts and lintel show inner depth. The roof-over-wall structure matches the house references. No isometric side faces appear, so the roof and wall both read as 3/4.

style.evidence: The thatch has about five ochre steps, per-course dark lines and tick-mark texture. The outline is dark brown, a tint of the neighbouring thatch and wood, not black. The wall planks are vertical, carry grain and highlights, and have round shield medallions. The stone footing is shaded, and the antler and skull ornament adds detail. The wall is a little plainer than the reference walls, and the roof courses repeat in a regular pattern, but the piece would sit acceptably beside the Beodeul houses.
